Ford Won't Sell Your Data, and Yes, You Can Still Make Your Smart Car Dumb Again
19 photos
Photo: Ford
Dumb cars have become smart cars with the arsenal of modern technology they’ve received in the last decade, but going back is now possible. Ford’s new Privacy Promise includes options to let users handle what data leaves their cars, and while drivers are put in control of their data, opting out comes with trade-offs. Major trade-offs, to be more precise, as certain big features will be lost once you prevent your car from talking to Ford .
This new Privacy Promise , whose role is to make it easier for drivers to understand what data is being shared with Ford, how the carmaker uses the data, and more importantly, how they can control what they share.
Ford insists on one particular aspect. The data you share with the company is being used to power certain capabilities, including connected services, so once you block the data sharing, your car is going to lose all these capabilities.
For example, the company says that vehicle diagnostics, driving characteristics, and your location are being used for real-time features like embedded navigation, traffic updates, and Roadside Assistance, and to diagnose vehicle issues.
But at the same time, Ford also touts a personalized experience that’s being built with your data, so the company will “offer products, features, and services that are uniquely tailored to you.”
Photo: Ford Because you’re always in control of this data-sharing process, you can block connected vehicle data from leaving your vehicle. “However, in doing so, some features like BlueCruise, Internet connectivity, and vehicle location data on the app will not be usable,” Ford says.
In other words, you’re going to lose all the new-generation features, turning your brand-new Ford into a dumb car again.
But Ford insists on one important part. “We never sell data about how you drive your vehicle to data brokers,” the carmaker says.
Your data is still being shared with others, though. Dealers, who need this data “for purposes such as helping with service, warranties, and supporting joint marketing activities,” are among those who work with Ford on this front. Ford’s partners in various spaces, such as customer support and marketing, will also be provided with your data.
What data Ford collects from your car Ford explains that in order to provide you with the full Connected Services and features experience, it’ll need to access the following data:
Vehicle data: the VIN, software version numbers, fuel and fluid levels, tire pressure, engine temperature, the odometer reading, maintenance, vehicle diagnostics, vehicle performance information Driving data: how the vehicle is operated and used - speed, the use of accelerator, brakes, steering, seatbelts Vehicle location: vehicle’s precise latitude and longitude Audio/visual and digital assistant data: images from forward-facing or rear-facing cameras, voice commands when the voice recognition system is in the “active listen” state
If you don’t want to share your location with Ford, you’ll lose the embedded navigation system, Roadside Assistance, the Ford Security package, and the ability to determine where you parked in the Ford app. You’ll still be able to access Android Auto and CarPlay and access the radio and listen to your media.
Photo: Ford The Connected features include software updates, remote features via the Ford app to lock and unlock your car, view the fuel and battery levels, and start and stop the engine. If you enable these features, you also get automatic alerts related to maintenance and be able to activate a Wi-Fi hotspot for up to 10 devices. Block the sharing of data related to Connected features, and you’re left with Android Auto, CarPlay, and a Bluetooth connection for phone calls and music.
Personalized features powered by your data include scheduled maintenance service notifications and other messages, as well as personalized offers “based on your vehicle usage and preferences.” All of these are gone if you block the sharing of data, so all it’s left is a direct communication channel with Ford about recalls, service, and safety.
Eventually, once the data sharing is enabled, you’ll get dealer- and service-related features, including the ability to find services and schedule an appointment with a nearby dealership. If you block the data sharing, you’ll have to do all of that online or directly with a dealer.
Photo: Ford Adjusting how the data sharing works is easy if you own a new-generation Ford. If your car is at least a 2018 model year, you should be able to access all privacy controls directly from the infotainment screen, so when you have a moment, just check out all these options (considering you’re aware of everything you’d be losing once you disable certain options).
Similar controls are also integrated into Ford’s mobile app. Ford says the new Privacy Promise is also applicable to Lincolns, but it will go live in the coming weeks. The same thing will happen for Ford customers in Mexico and Canada, and the carmaker says an expansion to other regions is already on the table, with more details to be shared shortly.

Samsung's One UI 9 Is Bad News for Android Auto Users, Google Has the Good News
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Samsung users have been battling Android Auto issues for as long as anyone can remember, and every single new Galaxy flagship ended up hitting the same connectivity problems . This time, it’s different. The connectivity problems aren’t caused by a new-generation smartphone but by a new-generation software update.
Samsung recently started rolling out One UI 9, the company’s latest and greatest software update that includes the update to Android 17 . Unsurprisingly, many users rushed to update their devices, as One UI 9 brings so many great configurations that all these users didn’t even care about the potential problems they could end up struggling with in their cars.
It turns out these problems are no longer potential but actually certain. Several users have been complaining that Android Auto doesn’t load after the update to One UI 9, and several others confirmed the same behavior in their cars.
Android Auto worked perfectly on One UI 8.5, many users revealed, but no longer fires up after the installation of the newly-released One UI 9.
In those rare cases where the app actually launches, Android Auto crashes in the middle of the drive due to what appears to be a connection loss.
The issues have already been reported with both wired and wireless connections, so while a random disconnect or a broken connection is typically caused by a bad cable, this isn’t the case here. Furthermore, users claim they’re using the same cord as they did before the update when everything was working correctly, so it wouldn’t make sense for the connection problems to be caused by a bad cord.
Users have already tried the typical workarounds in the Android Auto world, all to no avail. Clearing the cache of the Android Auto app, reinstalling it, and updating to the latest version doesn’t improve the experience, so many of these users are stuck with premium Android phones running the latest software versions without being able to run Android Auto.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Google: A fix is now available for One UI 9 users While a Google Community Specialist previously confirmed that reports of connection problems after the One UI 9 update had already been forwarded to the Android Auto team, it now looks like a fix is available.
Google has reportedly confirmed that the patch is now rolling out to Samsung phones running One UI 9, with the company promising that the issue will be fixed on all devices shortly.
The most recent Android Auto version is 18.1 . It started rolling out earlier this week through the Google Play Store, so if you don’t want to wait to get your hands on it - which could take up to several weeks - you can download and install it manually.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Big updates coming to Android Auto While Samsung users are eager to install new updates because they just want Android Auto to work, others have different reasons to be excited when new versions come out.
Android Auto is expected to receive the internally known as Cielo, the first major update since the introduction of Coolwalk in 2023 . With Cielo, Android Auto will get support for screens of all sizes, shapes, and resolutions, using the available screen estate more efficiently.
In terms of features, Android Auto will get support for widgets, and the long-term goal is to allow any widget that exists on Android phones to also become available in the car. Widgets will be displayed side-by-side with the rest of the Android Auto UI - and not on a separate screen, as it’s the case with CarPlay - and will allow users to get quick information, such as weather details and the next calendar appointments, without having to launch the full apps.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Android Auto will also unlock two new app categories: video apps and browsers. YouTube will pioneer the debut of video apps on Android Auto, allowing users to watch videos on their infotainment screens when their cars are stationary. The video playback will be restricted when vehicles start moving, and if the apps support it, an audio-only mode will automatically kick in.
This system should allow uninterrupted playback behind the wheel without causing the video to become a major source of distraction. For YouTube, the audio-only mode would require a Premium subscription, as it’ll use the ability to play audio in the background, a feature that is not part of the free tier.
Google hasn’t yet provided an ETA as to when all these new features could land, but the company recently reiterated that they would become available soon . The consensus is that the first beta users could get them by the end of the year, while the production rollout would start in the first quarter of 2027 and continue throughout the rest of the year. By the summer, we should all be able to watch YouTube videos on our Android Auto screens.

Nissan Seeks Adventures at 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas With Frontier, Pathfinder, Armada Concepts
8 photos
Photo: Nissan
The Japanese automaker says it has an unstoppable "commitment to extreme adventure and off-road thrills" and reveals these prototypes to back the claim at this year’s most important tuning and customization-related event in the United States.
The company has a bunch of cool news: the Formula E Team will enter Season 13 with drivers Oliver Rowland and Zane Maloney, alongside Sam Bird as its reserve and development driver and Abbi Pulling as its rookie and simulator driver for the 2026/27 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. And we also have important novelties for America.
There’s a new 2027 Nissan Pathfinder Special Edition to mark four decades of SUV heritage that reaches dealerships this month with a starting MSRP of $47,390 with FWD or $49,390 with Intelligent AWD. Also, the all-new 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid just went on sale in the US with the all-wheel drive SR with SR Technology Package grade, and its public debut is coming at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show, Nov. 20-29. Then there’s also the SEMA Show.
Nissan has initially tapped into the tuning enthusiast culture with the compact and sporty Sentra Spec V concept , a 300-hp compact sedan, as well as two Z models, the Nissan Project NAT2 SCCA Touring 2 and the Datsun S30 Concept. But now it’s time for some adventures off the beaten path. Thus, Nissan also returns to this year’s edition of the SEMA Show with a triumvirate of off-road concepts “that reimagine a new level of capability for the brand's most iconic trucks and SUVs.”
They were designed starting from the Frontier pickup truck, Pathfinder three-row SUV, and Armada full-size SUV and will be on display alongside the street concepts at the Nissan booth, #21521, in Central Hall at the Las Vegas Convention Center, Nov. 3-6. First, the Nissan Frontier Ronin concept is a vision of an “unstoppable off-road truck,” featuring a twin-turbocharged version of Frontier's 3.8-liter V6 engine.
There are also Nissan Titan suspension components to widen the vehicle's track width by 12 inches and lift it by over four inches, plus 35-inch Yokohama Geolandar X-AT tires on prototype 17-inch Nismo Ascend beadlock wheels. Last but not least, a full array of Nismo Off-Road accessories includes rock sliders, driving lights and a spare tire carrier, plus a custom big-brake kit, along with sport bucket seats, additional gauges for the twin-turbo engine and custom seat belts with topographic map-inspired details inside the cabin.
The Nissan Pathfinder celebrates its 40th anniversary, so the XE-V6 Concept taps into the celebrations by taking us back to the original WD21 model featuring retro "XE-V6" badging, red with black, charcoal and silver stripes exterior paint, a custom four-inch suspension lift kit, Yokohama Geolandar off-road tires on 18-inch prototype Nismo wheels, bespoke high-clearance off-road bumpers, a roof rack and plenty of additional accessories, including a rear-mounted swing-out tire carrier.
Last but not least, the Nissan Armada Jungle Patrol Concept is an expedition-style transformation with an open-roof design featuring a tubular roll cage plus inwards-facing seats that make it akin to a real safari vehicle. It rolls on 37-inch Yokohama Geolandar tires with custom long-travel suspension components, steel bumpers and fender flares, plus Nismo Off Road lights. So, what do you think, yay or nay? Also, which one of these three concepts is your favorite and why?

AAWireless Launches a Wireless Car Charger With Built-In Cooling, iPhone and Android Supported
7 photos
Photo: AAWireless
Wireless car chargers have been around for as long as anyone can remember, but contrary to what most people expect, choosing the right model is quite hard. Because the market is filled with such devices, and the number of companies building wireless chargers is mind-blowing, finding a device that works properly without overheating and delivers the promised charging speeds is quite a challenge.
Enter AAWireless.
The maker of the famous Android Auto wireless adapter has apparently decided it’s time to expand its product portfolio with the addition of a phone charger for cars.
Because AAWireless is all about a no-cord experience, the new charger, baptized simply AAWireless CHARGE, allows you to charge your phone wirelessly. No cables that must be connected to your phone are involved, though you’ll have to plug in the charger itself.
The bonus part is how this charger is built. Because wireless charging sometimes leads to overheating, which in turn leads to some phones prematurely triggering high temperature protections, AAWireless has integrated an active cooling system. A fan supposed to keep the charging temperature as low as possible is hiding under the case of the charger.
Photo: AAWireless The parent company promises that the fan isn’t making much noise, so the cabin should remain as quiet as possible even when the cooling system kicks in.
Otherwise, this new phone charger works like pretty much any similar product out there. You only need to snap your phone into place using built-in magnetic systems, such as MagSafe and PixelSnap. If your mobile device doesn’t come with such a magnetic attachment, that’s not a problem because AAWireless is also offering two magnetic rings that can be installed on your phone to be able to use the charger.
This means that your phone should be able to charge wirelessly with AAWireless CHARGE with and without MagSafe and Pixelsnap, assuming that wireless charging is supported. The device should work with pretty much any Qi2-compatible phone, delivering charging speeds of up to 25W.
The parent company recommends that you connect the charger to a 12V socket to reach that speed, but if you want to keep that one free and available for other car gadgets, you can always switch to a USB port. Just remember that unless your car delivers high charging speeds (which most cars don’t), your phone will charge slower.
Photo: AAWireless AAWireless CHARGE can be installed in your car in two different ways. The first - and the one I recommend, especially on sunny summer days - is directly in the air vent. The box includes a clamp that allows the charger to be installed securely into an air vent, assuming that the design of the air vent allows for such an approach in the first place.
The major benefit of this installation method is the extra cooling you'll get during the summer from the car’s air conditioning system. Cold air blowing directly into the charger and the phone prevents overheating (and faster battery degradation, for what it’s worth). However, you won’t want to use this method during cold winter days when you switch to hot air in your cabin.
In this case, you should be using the second installation method, which comes down to an adhesive dashboard base that allows you to install the CHARGE right in front of your eyes, typically above the infotainment screen on the console.
Photo: AAWireless Because of the integrated magnetic system, you just need to bring the phone close to the charger, and it’ll immediately snap into place, with the charging process automatically kicking in.
Before you ask, here’s the bad news: the charger doesn’t integrate an Android Auto wireless adapter , but this is certainly an idea that should land on the parent company’s roadmap. However, if your phone is connected to the wireless charger, it can very well work with a separate AAWireless adapter. So if you also have a dongle plugged in, charging your phone using AAWireless CHARGE won’t interrupt your connection.
The box includes everything to get you started with this adapter. In addition to the obvious 12V charger to power the charger if you don’t want to rely on USB power, you also get a wireless magnetic mount, an air vent clamp, an adhesive dashboard base, a USB-C to USB-C cable, and 2 magnetic ring adapters.
Photo: AAWireless There’s no USB-A cable or adapter, so if you want to use the USB power option and your car is fitted with a standard USB port, you’ll have to bring your own cable or USB-A to USB-C adapter.
As for the price, this new product from AAWireless isn’t the most affordable, but it’s not expensive either. It can be yours for $49.99 in most markets where the company’s Android Auto wireless adapters are already available, including Europe and the United States. It doesn’t seem to be live on Amazon just yet, but you can order it from the official AAWireless page .

Saab has tested AI agents on the company's Gripen E multirole fighter jet (Saab)
BELFAST — Swedish manufacturer Saab has unveiled a suite of inhouse AI agents designed for future aircraft platforms, following testing of the new technologies on a Gripen E multirole fighter jet.
The move demonstrates the firm’s “ability to develop, train, and fly its own Al for air combat” operations, according to a company statement released today.
The company added that the agents use “various Al techniques to master tactical decision-making in complex operational environments.” They can also work with a pilot inside a cockpit or from its own uncrewed air vehicle.
Key to the autonomous project is Saab’s AI Fighter Jet Pilot Academy, designed to develop the agents and, in parallel, establish infrastructure necessary to “create, train and evaluate” them, noted the Saab statement.
“The harder question is how we turn this success [of flying with the agents] into a dependable capability that can learn, improve, and be relevant over time,” Peter Nilsson, head of Advanced Programs at Saab’s aeronautics unit, told Breaking Defense and other media ahead of the announcement. “[T]hat is the true purpose of the AI Fighter Pilot Academy.”
He stressed that the “strategic advantage” of producing AI-driven data, “increasingly comes from reducing the distance between experience, learning, and field-led capability.”
It is of “enormous value to have a software-driven fighter like Gripen who can cope with this [computer processing] speed,” added Nilsson.
To date, the AI agents have predominately been tested and integrated with the fighter jet under Beyond Visual Range (BVR) combat conditions, much like a similar flight test campaign from 2025 , when Helsing’s Centaur AI tool was used to take control of the fighter jet and autonomously complete a number of BVR maneuvers. Longer term however, Saab plans on leveraging the inhouse AI technology to advance development of its future air programs. As Breaking Defense previously reported , the manufacturer is developing a trio of unmanned aircraft — the A1, A2 and A3 — on the path toward the design of a new loyal wingman drone.
The company’s latest foray into AI-based Gripen testing follows a handful of similar flight tests in 2025 when Helsing’s Centaur AI tool was used to take control of the fighter jet and autonomously complete a number of BVR maneuvers.
Meanwhile, in an effort to scale computer capacity for the AI agents, the firm has also decided to become partial founder in a Swedish government-backed initiative dubbed Sferical Al.
Nilsson said that without Sferical AI, “otherwise you have to go to Google or Amazon … and pay some money” meaning, “you maybe don’t have full control of your data.”
To retain such a capability in Sweden is “enormous” for Saab, he added, noting that the new initiative was formally inaugurated during a ceremony in Stockholm last month.
Per a Saab slide shared by Nilsson, Sferical Al is built using Nvidia’s DGX SuperPOD architecture that makes it possible to develop Large Language Model and Vision-Language Model capabilities to aid agent and operator communications.
When Sferical Al is applied to a one-hour simulated training flight, it can produce the equivalent of one billion flight hours for a human pilot. “The exponential [computational] curve is … really hard to comprehend,” explained Nilsson.

SRT Performance Joins the 2026 SEMA Show Featuring the First-Ever Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept
15 photos
Photo: Jeep
The Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept, prepared for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, is the first model from specialty brand Jeep with an SRT badge – more could be on the horizon in the coming years.
Jeep has been pretty busy lately, as it strives to bring out enough novelties to snatch the leadership among Stellantis brands in America back from Ram Trucks. So, we have seen what’s new about the 2027 Compass, 2027 Gladiator, 2027 Wrangler, 2027 Cherokee, the new 35-inch Tire Launch Edition for the Gladiator, or the 2027 Switchback that completes the year-long Twelve 4 Twelve series for the Wrangler nameplate, as well as Jeep being named the official 4x4 of the city of Moab.
And that was all in October 2026 alone! Now, Stellantis is kicking off November for the Jeep brand with the reveal of the Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept, the first concept model from Jeep wearing the SRT badge as it reimagines the American off-road icon. This prototype obviously pays tribute as it reimagines the legendary Jeep CJ-8 Scrambler with a combination of “open-air freedom, pickup versatility, authentic Jeep capability and unmistakable SRT attitude.”
It was developed starting from a Jeep Wrangler SUV foundation, rather than the Gladiator pickup truck sibling, and the “concept channels the original Scrambler’s spirit of adventure and individuality” via new proportions, a rugged utility flair, and “an uncompromising SRT performance vision.” This is a high-speed desert runner, a true V8-powered off-road beast.
“The original Scrambler became an icon because it broke the rules. It looked different, worked differently, and represented a certain kind of freedom that resonated with enthusiasts then and still does today,” said Tim Kuniskis, head of American Brands, SRT Performance and Direct Connection division, Stellantis North America. The new version is a two-door pickup with a usable truck bed and completely throws the Wrangler rule book out the window by packing the first independent front suspension ever offered on a Wrangler.
The bespoke high-travel independent front suspension, developed with off-road racing champion Casey Currie, is mixed with a trophy-truck-inspired rear axle, a heavy-duty wheel package, and desert-racing-focused hardware. There are also longer doors than on a Wrangler, a bespoke rear, an integrated pickup bed, a tailgate, bespoke fender flares, and a structural roll cage, along with Punk’n orange paint, bronze beadlock wheels, and SRT touches.
Under the hood, the company strapped in the 6.4-liter Hemi V8, but the concept is mostly about future hardware rather than a preview of an upcoming production truck. Alas, it does come with an integrated pickup bed and custom rear-seat system to switch between cargo and passenger-carrying capabilities, and the rear seats clip directly into floor-mounted hooks and can be completely removed or faced toward the front or the rear.
Inside, the cockpit has performance-focused seats, Dark Graphite leather, orange inserts, contrast stitching, bronze accents, and SRT embroidery, as well as custom grab handles, trim treatments, and a rear-seat Jeep Multi-panel System. So, what do you think – yay or nay?

2026 SEMA Show • Nissan Seeks Adventures at 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas With Frontier, Pathfinder, Armada Concepts
Audi’s Upcoming 2028 RS6 Avant Gets a Virtual Tuning Job
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project
It’s been one a half years since production of the all-new sixth-generation Audi A6 kicked off, yet there is still no RS 6 in the company’s lineup. However, that’s about to change, as the four-ring brand’s Sport division is putting the final touches on the range-topping version of the series.
Unlike its predecessors, which were only available as five-door station wagons, the all-new RS 6 will be offered in two body styles. The four-door sedan will join the Avant for the first time since the C6. The latter model was launched at the Frankfurt Motor Show back in 2007, with production starting that same year and ending in 2011. It was based on the same nuts and bolts as the era’s A6, as well as the S6 and A6 allroad quattro.
As for the all-new Audi RS 6 , it will utilize the PPC (Premium Platform Combustion) bones. Thus, it will have a lot of things in common not only with the lesser A6 family, but also the smaller A5 (B10), the latest Q5, the new-generation Q7, and the first-ever Q9. The construction is therefore on the versatile side of things, as it can accommodate plenty of models, from premium compact vehicles to full-size SUVs.
It is yet unknown when the upcoming RS 6 will go official, as Audi has yet to announce the unveiling date, though from what we can tell, we are probably months away (or is that weeks?) from seeing it under the spotlight, with no camouflage on its body. Chances are it will probably arrive at dealers across the United States of America for the 2028 model year, and the automaker is expected to offer it in both body styles (Sedan and Avant).
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project Now, if the official unveiling of the all-new Audi RS 6 hasn’t taken place yet, then how has this model been visited by the tuning fairy? Well, it’s a virtual visit, as mentioned in the title. The renderings came from @ildar_project on Instagram, and they portray the model with a more aggressive body kit. Chances are we will eventually see some similar builds once the model goes official, as numerous tuners will offer all kinds of upgrades for it.
For now, this CGI-tuned new-gen Audi RS 6 Avant sports an entirely new hood that is on the vented side of things. The large splitter with blades on the sides is also new, and there are some add-ons surrounding the vents on each side of the grille, as well as yellow daytime running lights, which are part of the virtual makeover. The door mirror casings have also come from the CGI tuning game, just like the side skirts.
The wheel arches appear to be a bit wider than on the stock car, and further back, this imagined Audi RS 6 Avant has a pair of spoilers above and below the rear windscreen. There is also a new diffuser with a motorsport-like extra brake light in the middle, as well as cutouts for the RS signature dual oval tailpipes. The car sits closer to the ground than usual, rides on large concave wheels with a Y-spoke design, and has a satin green look on the outside, as well as some forged carbon accents.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project The usual RS logos decorate its exterior, which also sports some black details for more contrast, and while the interior hasn’t opened up in these digital illustrations, we already know what we are looking at, because it will be virtually identical to that of the new-gen A6. Well, save for the front bucket seats, the dedicated load screens and submenus on the displays, the steering wheel, trim and upholstery, and some other bits and bobs, as these will draw a clear line between the A6 and the RS 6.
Moreover, a reworked chassis setup will also be part of the real RS makeover, alongside a set of beefier brakes. The latter are a must in order to keep the power in check. Previous information claimed that the new RS 6 might get the plug-in hybrid V8 assembly from the Bentley Continental GT Speed, which is officially good for 771 hp (782 ps/575 kW).
However, new data suggests that we might be looking at a V6 with electric assistance, and it could be the same setup used on the new RS 5 . This model has a twin-turbo 2.9-liter V6 mill that is good for 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW), and the electric motor is rated at 174 hp (177 ps/130 kW). The total output stands at 630 hp (639 ps/470 kW), enabling 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 3.6 seconds. The RS 5 has a roughly 50-mile (80 km) electric driving range with the 22 kWh battery pack fully charged.
Audi’s upcoming RS 6 will likely offer more oomph, and the rumor mill speaks about 740 hp (750 ps/552 kW ) or so in total. Guess we will find out if that’s true when the model premieres. But if you had to choose between the next-gen RS 6 and the current BMW M5, which one would you get and why? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ильдар (@ildar_project)

Ringbrothers Mesmerizes the SEMA Show Once Again, This Time With Billie, the 650-HP Pontiac GTO
12 photos
Photo: ringbrothers / Instagram
Ringbrothers is one of the best-known American custom car builders and aftermarket parts manufacturers, founded and run by brothers Jim and Mike Ring out of Spring Green, Wisconsin.
Their roots date back to the 1990s, and today the company is widely recognized for its high-end restomod build projects, completing just a handful of custom flagship vehicles every year, allowing for obsessive attention to detail in the meantime. Despite their ultra-luxury status, they remain tied with the local community, functioning as an While world-famous for their radical custom builds, the shop also functions as a local community auto body and collision repair shop.
As per tradition, Ringbrothers is often associated with the SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, where they often unveil the radical custom creations. So, this year at the Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) Show in Las Vegas, the star of the red carpet for Ringbrothers is Billie, which continues the tradition of cool names like Octavia (a restomod 1971 Aston Martin DBS with an 800-hp Ford Coyote V8), Kingpin (a 1969 Ford Mustang Mach 1 drenched in carbon fiber and 3D-printed stuff), Recoil the 1964 Chevrolet Chevelle or Defiant, a heavily modified 1972 AMC Javelin AMX.
Now, for the 2026 SEMA Show edition, the headliner is Billie, a custom-built 1965 Pontiac GTO Convertible that was painstakingly created over more than 5,500 hours of work from an old Pontiac Tempest Convertible into a 650-hp GTO with a five-inch-wider body and a ton of new stuff all over the place. They said the ‘goat’ has jumped the fence, so after “more than 5,500 hours of meticulous craftsmanship, extensive fabrication and modern performance” transformation, the 1965 Pontiac Tempest Convertible turned into Billie.
Aside from the five-inch-wider body, there are also carbon-fiber doors with reshaped front fenders, widened rear quarters, and lengthened rocker panels, “enhancing the Pontiac's original proportions while retaining its iconic silhouette.” Of course, the morphing wouldn’t be complete without the complementary, custom BASF Glasurit “Billie Goat Blue” finish, which is seconded by polished chrome accents and contrasting black details.
“Billie began as a tribute to a GTO once owned by our client's mother, who received the original car as a gift,” said Ringbrothers co-owner Mike Ring. “The owner wanted to recreate something that held real sentimental value, and during our early conversations, he suggested calling it GOAT. We came back with Billie, as in Billy goat, and that moniker stuck. It's a playful nod to the GTO's heritage, but more, a deeply personal tribute to a car with a special place in his family's history.”
The redesign of the exterior also includes a bespoke carbon-fiber hood with an enlarged scoop, precision-machined billet-aluminum inserts, and functional vents. More carbon-fiber components include the front wheel tubs, lower front valance, as well as the rear diffuser with its integrated exhaust ducts, while the team also made custom bumpers and redesigned the headlight surrounds, among other things. There was also extensive fabrication done to the floor, trunk, firewall, and transmission tunnel.
Under the hood resides a Wegner Motorsports supercharged 6.2-liter LT4 V8 packing a punch with 650 hp and 650 lb-ft of torque, and the power is routed through a Bowler Performance 10-speed automatic transmission while the soundtrack comes from a bespoke Ringbrothers exhaust featuring Flowmaster components. Under the stunning body resides a Roadster Shop Fast Track Stag III chassis complemented by Fox coilovers and six-piston Brembo brakes.
The Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires are shod around staggered 19- and 20-inch HRE Performance G-Code wheels, and the interior is dressed with a complementary gray-and-blue leather setup and features a redesigned dashboard that was repositioned four inches forward and two inches lower. It also has custom-machined aluminum trim, Dakota Digital instruments, Vintage Air climate control, and a Gentex auto-dimming rearview mirror.
The restored factory radio actually hides Bluetooth connectivity, and an unexpected handcrafted detail comes from an olive wood espresso portafilter-inspired shifter. So, what do you think – it’s cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ringbrothers (@ringbrothers)

Better Late Than Never: All-New VW T-Roc Is Coming to Australia in Early 2027, Almost Two Years Late
6 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The second generation of the Volkswagen T-Roc subcompact crossover SUV was introduced in August 2025, but it will probably take almost two years to get to the Land Down Under. Well, at least it wasn’t sacrificed on the altar of business recuperation.
There’s no denying – the second largest global automaker, Volkswagen AG, is going through a rough patch. Just recently we heard that the company stopped the development of the ID. Golf because they can’t “afford it” anymore; wage talks with the workers at home in Germany collapsed in October, and the company might face a strike in January 2027, and Volkswagen, plus Audi and Porsche, continued to lose hard-earned sales in the United States during the third quarter of the year.
Every region and market is now more important than ever, so it’s a good thing that Volkswagen Australia has confirmed that the all-new Volkswagen T-Roc will finally arrive at local dealerships in early 2027, “ushering in the next chapter for one of the brand's most successful nameplates.” The Volkswagen T-Roc was originally introduced globally at the 2017 Frankfurt Motor Show and launched in November 2017, almost a decade ago on the Volkswagen Group MQB A1 platform.
Generally considered the SUV companion of the iconic VW Golf, the T-Roc resides in the small space between the T-Cross and the Tiguan, with the second iteration launched in August 2025 based on the premium MQB Evo platform shared with the Golf Mk8.5, among others. According to VW Australia, the “next-generation model builds on the strengths that have made the T-Roc a customer favourite, introducing mild-hybrid technology, a more sophisticated design and significant advances in technology, safety and comfort.”
Volkswagen’s newest styling language and enhanced lighting signatures underpin the fresh exterior, and inside customers will discover an upgraded cabin with Volkswagen's latest-generation digital technologies. The T-Roc range comes with mild hybrid technology for the first time in Australia, but the new model also comes with more interior space and additional practical features.
There is also Volkswagen's latest infotainment system, a new generation of driver assistance technologies and a big range of comfort-focused features. However, additional information, including local pricing, model specifications, as well as Australian equipment details, will be announced at a later date closer to the market arrival.
Currently, the global model features both front-wheel drive and all-wheel drive setups and is powered by the company’s ubiquitous 1.5-liter TSI gasoline engine and a seven-speed DSG transmission with mild hybrid 48-volt assistance. Most likely the Australian model will mirror this setup when it goes on sale in the market sometime next year.
“Our Volkswagen T-Roc has become one of Volkswagen Australia's most successful and popular models, resonating strongly with customers looking for a compact SUV with genuine character, style and everyday versatility. The all-new generation builds on the qualities that have made the T-Roc such a success in Australia, while delivering meaningful advances in design, technology, comfort, safety and efficiency,” said Piergiorgio Minto, Brand Director of Volkswagen Passenger Vehicles.
